sights.address: Former palace site, Bidadari estate (off Upper Serangoon Road / Mount Vernon Road), Singapore
sights.w: The estate and the whole Bidadari district take their name from this vanished palace. British engineer Henry Minchin Simons acquired the 45-acre grounds in 1855; Sultan Abu Bakar of Johor bought it in the 1860s and gifted it to his second wife, the Danish-born Sultana Zubaidah (Cecilia Catharina Lange) — its beauty likened to a 'bidadari' (Malay/Sanskrit for celestial nymph or angel). After Zubaidah moved to Johor the palace was rented out, then demolished in 1915; its name outlived it, passing to the cemetery and today's estate.

A Hindu temple to Shiva and the goddess Durga, first erected in 1906 near the Lavender Street / Rumah Miskin junction and shifted three times — via Beatty Road — before settling in Potong Pasir in 1982. Demolished in 2014 for water-leakage and space problems and rebuilt in Dravidian style at a cost of S$2.7 million, it was reconsecrated on 4 December 2016, with chambers for Ganesha, Murugan, Shiva, Durga, Lakshmi and Saraswati.

sights.address: Former garden site, Bidadari (Woodleigh / Upper Aljunied vicinity), Singapore
sights.w: The green ancestor of today's Alkaff Lake: from 1929/30 to 1964 the wealthy Hadhrami-Arab Alkaff family ran a magnificent Japanese-style pleasure garden east of the Bidadari Cemetery — artificial hills, tea houses and a large ornamental lake landscaped with Japanese help. It closed and was cleared in the 1960s (the site now around Cedar Girls' Secondary), but its memory is deliberately echoed by the Alkaff Lake completed in Bidadari Park in 2024.
